title: Prescriptions Training Note: Days on Hand from the Last Refill before a Travel Refill
content:
Before a travel refill of a Kestrel Prescriptions record, the vacation override on-hand days measure how much of the most recent refill the patient still holds; they are the days of medication on hand that the vacation override days supply deducts.

## The rule

The vacation override on-hand days are worked out by the first case that fits, the pickup being the pickup entry that names the most recent refill:

1. **Picked up on a later day than it was dispensed:** the refill's days supply dispensed less the calendar days from that pickup date, as day 0, to today, never below zero.
2. **Not picked up:** its whole days supply dispensed counts as on hand.
3. **Otherwise** (picked up on the day it was dispensed): its days supply dispensed less the calendar days from its dispensing date, as day 0, to today, never below zero.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical refill of 30 days dispensed on day 0, today is day 12)

| Pickup of that refill | Case | On-hand days |
|---|---|---|
| day 5 | 1 | 30 less 7: 23 |
| never picked up | 2 | 30 |
| day 0 | 3 | 30 less 12: 18 |
| day 3, with today day 40 | 1 | 30 less 37, never below zero: 0 |

## Questions answered

**The refill sat in will-call and was collected a week later.** It was picked up on a later day than it was dispensed, so the count runs from the pickup date.

**Which refill is looked at?** The most recent refill on the prescription.
